ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, a right-angled triangle is placed with point C located on the extension of $FD$, $AB \parallel CF$, $\angle F = \angle ACB = 90^\circ$, $\angle E = 30^\circ$, and $\angle A = 45^\circ$. What is the measure of $\angle CBD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given: $\because$ $\angle A=45^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle ABC=45^\circ$,\\
$\because$ $AB\parallel CF$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle BCD=45^\circ$,\\
$\because$ $\angle E=30^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle EDF=60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle BDC=180^\circ-\angle EDF=120^\circ$\\
In $\triangle BCD$, $\angle BCD=45^\circ$, $\angle BDC=120^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle CBD=180^\circ-\angle BDC-\angle BCD=15^\circ$,\\
Therefore, the answer is: $\boxed{15^\circ}$.

method.method_draft: Angle-chase through triangle BCD. From the image, identify that E, B, D are collinear, F, D, C are collinear on the same horizontal baseline, and B, C, A form the right triangle with the right angle at C. From the text, use AB parallel CF, angle F = angle ACB = 90°, angle E = 30°, and angle A = 45°. Since triangle ABC has a right angle at C and angle A = 45°, angle ABC = 45°. Because AB is parallel to CF and C, D, F are collinear, transfer this angle to get angle BCD = 45°. In right triangle EFD, angle E = 30° and angle F = 90°, so angle EDF = 60°. Since DB is the same line as DE and DC is the opposite ray to DF, angle BDC = 180° - 60° = 120°. Finally, in triangle BCD, compute angle CBD = 180° - 120° - 45° = 15°.

Finally, in triangle BCD, ∠CBD=180°-∠BDC-∠BCD=180°-120°-45°=15°.
